title: wg-easy · VPN operations
description: Multi-interface VPN traffic, recent client connectivity, routing-group policy health and exit-candidate observability using the existing wg-easy exporter.

panels.title: Metrics endpoint
panels.description: Prometheus scrape success only. A successful scrape is not proof of tunnel or Internet reachability.

panels.title: Enabled interfaces observed up
panels.description: Filtered by Interface. Observed device state, not external UDP reachability.

panels.title: Enabled clients
panels.description: Filtered by Interface and Client.

panels.title: Enabled clients with recent handshake
panels.description: Enabled peers with a handshake less than 10 minutes old. Idle peers can appear disconnected. Filtered by Interface and Client.

targets.expr: sum((max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_client_connected{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"})) * on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}))

panels.title: Enabled groups not verified active
panels.description: Filtered by Routing group only. Zero is healthy; no data is not zero.

panels.title: Global reconciliation degraded
panels.description: Global coordinator state. Also check revision backlog and per-interface health below.

options.content:
**Traffic is measured at the server.** Client upload = peer → server; client download = server → peer. Exit peer traffic also includes forwarding, so summing members and exits counts the routed path twice.

**Filters:** Interface + Client apply to client panels; Routing group applies to group health and exit candidate panels; Interface also limits exit candidates. Global reconciliation and scrape health stay instance-wide. **Recent handshake ≠ end-to-end health.** Gaps mean missing data. Routing-group byte attribution and per-group selected exits are not exposed by this exporter.

panels.title: Peer-side throughput · all selected peers
panels.description: Sum of selected peer counters. Includes exit forwarding when exits are selected; not unique Internet usage. rate() is calculated before aggregation and handles observed counter resets.

targets.expr: 8 * sum(sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (rate(wireguard_received_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}[$__rate_interval])))

8 * sum(sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (rate(wireguard_sent_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Client connectivity over time
panels.description: The application uses a fixed 10-minute handshake threshold. Disabled clients are excluded from recent-handshake and stale counts.

targets.expr: sum((max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_client_connected{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"})) * on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}))

sum(wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}) - sum((max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_client_connected{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"})) * on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}))

panels.title: Top 10 upload volumes · selected time range
panels.description: Estimated transferred bytes during the selected range, not lifetime counters. Counter resets are handled; missed scrapes, label changes and unseen resets can undercount. Includes whole-peer traffic for exit clients.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (increase(wireguard_received_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Top 10 download volumes · selected time range
panels.description: Estimated transferred bytes during the selected range, not lifetime counters. Counter resets are handled; missed scrapes, label changes and unseen resets can undercount. Includes whole-peer traffic for exit clients.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (increase(wireguard_sent_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Client state history
panels.description: Disabled takes precedence over an old/recent handshake. The recent threshold is 10 minutes; sleeping clients are not necessarily faulty.

targets.expr: (wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}) * on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (1 + (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_client_connected{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"})))

panels.title: Current client inventory
panels.description: Enabled is configuration; Recent handshake is the exporter’s observation, which may briefly persist after disabling. An address identifies the client profile, not its current public endpoint.

panels.title: Time since last observed handshake
panels.description: Computed from timestamps at query time. Clients with no observed handshake are absent here and listed alongside.

targets.expr: sort_desc(max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (time() - wireguard_latest_handshake_timestamp_seconds{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}",client_id=~"${client:regex}"}))

panels.title: Enabled clients with no observed handshake
panels.description: No current handshake timestamp. This can mean never connected, a recreated interface, or unavailable peer runtime data. Empty is expected when every enabled client has a timestamp.

panels.title: Routing-group state history
panels.description: Active means the latest desired policy is verified. No selected exit covers awaiting_exit, blocked and host_fallback; these cannot be distinguished with current metrics. Group health ignores Interface and Client filters.

panels.title: Configured members per group
panels.description: Configured membership count, not the number online. No membership-to-client mapping is exported.

options.content:
### Per-group member traffic is not available
The current exporter provides neither client-to-group membership nor routing-rule byte counters. A truthful member-traffic total per group therefore cannot be calculated. Even with membership labels, summing client traffic would measure **all traffic of the members**, not just traffic matching routed prefixes.

Below, choose a **Routing group** to inspect the **whole-peer traffic of its configured exit candidates**. Shared exits appear once; their bytes are not attributed to the selected group. Primary and backup candidates are both included.

panels.title: Exit clients · candidates for selected routing groups
Traffic sent to exit peers · server → exit
panels.description: Whole-peer server TX, typically including forwarded member uploads. Filters to configured candidates, not only active exits. Includes traffic from other groups and the exit’s own traffic.

targets.expr: 8 * ((sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (rate(wireguard_sent_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0)))

panels.title: Traffic received from exit peers · exit → server
panels.description: Whole-peer server RX, typically including return traffic to members. Shared candidates are deduplicated by job, instance, interface and client ID. No per-group byte attribution.

targets.expr: 8 * ((sum by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (rate(wireguard_received_bytes{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0)))

panels.title: Exit candidate handshake history
panels.description: Uses the generic 10-minute client threshold, not the routing health timeout. A recent handshake alone does not prove an exit is eligible or selected.

targets.expr: (wg_easy_client_enabled{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} * on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (1 + (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_client_connected{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"})))) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0))

panels.title: Configured exit priority by group
panels.description: Lower priority is preferred. Configuration only: the exporter does not identify the selected exit for each group. Client filter does not apply.

panels.title: Active group count per exit · all groups
panels.description: The Routing group filter selects candidate clients, but each exported count covers ALL groups for that exit. This runtime count does not independently prove the latest desired revision is active; use group health above.

targets.expr: (wg_easy_exit_client_active_groups{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"}) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0))

panels.title: Configured groups depending on exit · all groups
panels.description: Includes primary/backup candidacy and disabled groups. Count covers all configured groups, even when a single group is selected.

targets.expr: (wg_easy_exit_client_groups{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"}) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0))

panels.title: Configured members depending on exit · all groups
panels.description: Potential dependency count across all groups configuring this exit. Not active forwarding clients; not additive across primary/backup exits.

targets.expr: (wg_easy_exit_client_members{job="$job",instance="$instance",interface=~"${interface:regex}"}) and on (job, instance, interface, client_id) (max by (job, instance, interface, client_id, client_name) (wg_easy_exit_client_candidate_priority{job="$job",instance="$instance",group_id=~"${group:regex}",interface=~"${interface:regex}"} >= bool 0))

panels.title: Interface observed state
panels.description: Enabled and observed-up state only. Does not prove configuration convergence or published UDP reachability.

panels.title: Interface revision backlog
panels.description: Desired minus applied revision. Zero means no revision backlog; check degraded and restart-required flags separately.

panels.title: Time since last successful reconcile
panels.description: Informational: an idle system may not need a new reconcile. No data means there is no successful timestamp, or the metric is unavailable. No age-based failure threshold is implied.
